newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada rules out rescue for Canadian Air.
newsitem.headline: Canada rules out rescue for Canadian Air.

text.p: Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien reiterated on Wednesday that his government has no intention of rescuing cash-strapped Canadian Airlines Corp.

"They have to resolve the problem internally," Chretien told reporters during a stopover in Vancouver en route to a summit of Pacific Rim leaders in Manila. He noted that the company itself has not asked for government funding.

"We're all anxious that they find a solution...The problem is to make this company profitable. A loan will not make the company profitable. A loan is just extending the survival of the company for months or years," Chretien said.
The airline is negotiating with its unions on a restructuring plan that calls for a 10 percent wage cut.

It has warned that unless workers agree to the plan by the end of November it will be forced to cease operations early next year. Some union officials have called on the federal government to aid the airline.
